headline: Catch-up review (last run Aug 31, covering the Sep 1 + Sep 2 sessions): KSE-100 down two straight sessions (−1.24% cumulative) as the US and Iran exchanged fresh strikes and Iran moved to effectively close the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping — a real oil-supply-shock escalation, not just diplomatic tension; Brent jumped to ~$95.68. Portfolio value ~Rs 10.18M, P/L +Rs 139K (+1.38% on cost), down from +2.22% (Rs 223K) on Aug 31 — broad market-driven, not a single-name blowup. GLAXO (−8.1% on cost) and SEARL (+1.5%, but down ~5% this week) both sold off harder than the market; likely driver is a new DRAP drug-pricing framework review (margins near 40% under scrutiny, tighter hardship-policy rules being drafted) — a sector regulatory watch item, not yet a company-specific cut. EFERT bucked the selloff, up ~5% over the two sessions to Rs 190.36 on firm urea pricing ('urea will not get cheaper' — Engro management, Aug 5) despite the broader market being down. AVN's Aug 25 EXIT call remains unexecuted (24,500 shares still held) — no new news, thesis unchanged (H1 FY26 net loss). No holding crossed a notification threshold (KSE-100 daily move stayed under 2.5%, drawdown under 10%).
market: KSE-100 closed Wed Sep 2 at 174,776.60, down 1,690.40 pts (−0.96%) from Tue's 176,466.99, which itself was down slightly from Mon Aug 31's 176,975.67 — cumulative −1.24% over two sessions. Driver: the US and Iran exchanged fresh strikes overnight into Sep 2, following tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday; Iran's IRGC said the US strikes would further restrict Hormuz traffic, which carries roughly a fifth of global oil consumption — genuine supply-disruption risk, not just posturing. Oil jumped in response (Brent ~$95.68, WTI ~$90.83). For an oil-importing economy like Pakistan this is a real macro risk (import bill, PKR, inflation) if it persists — worth watching closely over the next few sessions rather than dismissing as routine geopolitical noise. Selling was broad-based (356 of 501 traded names down) hitting autos, cement, banks, OMCs, E&P and power. Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) widened from ~6.6% (Aug 31) to ~7.8% today — getting closer to, but still short of, the 10% line that would justify deploying the AICF/MICF cash reserve into MZNPETF/MIIETF; if the Hormuz situation escalates further this could move quickly. Backdrop otherwise unchanged: SBP holding at 11.5% since the Jul 27 pause, no new SBP/IMF news this review. NEW: a government-directed DRAP review of the drug-pricing framework (Aug 28-29 news) is examining pharma margins run 'around 40%' and could tighten the Hardship Policy and pricing-formula rules — this is a plausible driver behind GLAXO and SEARL underperforming the broader selloff this week (both down ~5% over 2-3 sessions vs the index's ~1%); nothing enacted yet, just a policy review to track into Q4. EFERT — no negative news; Engro's public line since Aug 5 has been 'urea will not get cheaper,' i.e. holding the price umbrella rather than discounting into the glut, and DAP inventory (53K tons, sourced from Morocco) gives it room; stock actually rose to Rs 190.36, bucking the market. MEBL — no new dividend or negative news; Meezan crossed Rs 4B disbursed under the government's Ghar Ho Tu Apna housing-finance scheme (Rs 2.2B in August alone) and congratulated the Ministry of Finance on Pakistan's first sovereign hybrid sukuk — supportive but not a catalyst; today's price dip is market-wide, not company-specific. FABL — checked again, still no published ex-date for the Aug 6 Rs 1.50/share interim. AVN — no new news since the Aug 28 H1 filing; EXIT call unexecuted through 6 reviews now. DATA QUALITY: stock prices refreshed normally (multiple commits both sessions). Fund NAVs (funds_updated: Aug 13) are now 20 days stale — the MUFAP scraper issue remains unresolved; ~30% of the portfolio's value (all 7 funds) is being priced off a 3-week-old NAV snapshot, which is a growing blind spot and needs a real fix.

actions.title: Avanceon — H1 report confirms swing to a real net loss; EXIT call now backed by hard numbers, still unexecuted
actions.detail: No new news since the Aug 28 H1/Q2 FY26 filing: consolidated H1 2026 revenue grew a healthy +34% YoY (Rs 7.04B) but the company swung from a Rs 168M profit to a Rs 260M NET LOSS (EPS −Rs 0.62 vs +Rs 0.38); Q2 alone the loss widened to Rs 317M (EPS −Rs 0.74) from a Rs 104M loss a year earlier. Standalone tells the same story (H1 swung from +Rs 136M profit to −Rs 66M loss). No dividend declared (NIL). Cause: admin/selling expenses up 45% YoY, far outpacing revenue growth, plus 'other income' that cushioned last year's profit (Rs 162M in H1 2025) collapsed to Rs 77M this year, exposing weak core operating economics. This is real, board-confirmed deterioration — not a rumor or a single bad line item. Now Rs 29.10, −35.4% on cost, giving back the Aug 31 bounce. No further earnings catalyst is pending before Q3; there is no reason left to keep waiting. The Aug 25 EXIT call is unexecuted through 6 reviews now — recommend selling the entire position at market.
actions.target: Sell all 24,500 shares at market (~Rs 29) — proceeds ~Rs 712K, split ~55% into MEBL (~Rs 392K), ~45% into MZNPETF (~Rs 320K)
